title: Evaluation-defined internal Hom pullback is invertible for a perfect source
statement: Let g:T→X be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and M,K∈D(O_X) [def-pc-derived-category] with M perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex]. Let t be a natural tensor/pullback isomorphism whose forward maps satisfy IsCanonicalPullbackTensorComparison [def-pc-derived-pullback-tensor-comparison]. Use the fixed normalized tensor-Hom adjunctions b_X,b_T [def-pc-affine-global-hom-base-change-map]. Then the map Lg*RHom(M,K)→RHom(Lg*M,Lg*K) obtained by transposing t.inv_(RHom(M,K),M);Lg*(b_X(M).counit_K) under b_T(Lg*M) is invertible. Internal Hom and pullback are [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, def-pc-derived-pullback]. No quasi-coherence or boundedness assumption on K is needed.

source.place: Remark 08I3, evaluation-defined comparison; Example 0FPC, perfect duality

proof.text: Equip M with quasi-coherent cohomology by perfectness. Obtain the tensor-Hom bijections and their naturality on X. Apply perfect_rhom_tensor_comparison with both quasi-coherent inputs M, extracting its ExactPairing M D; the object K is not used in this step and is not assumed quasi-coherent.

Realize the forward comparison t.hom as the inverse tensorator of a CoreMonoidal structure m on derivedPullback g by canonicalPullbackTensor_monoidal_realization. Iso.ext applied to the inverse tensorator equation proves t.inv equals the monoidal tensorator. Install m.toMonoidal locally in the proof.

The upstream theorem tensorRightAdjunction_counit_app expands the counit of tensorRightAdjunction M D as associator, evaluation, and right unitor. The proved private helper monoidal_rigid_counit uses ExactPairing.map and the monoidal map_associator, map_whiskerLeft and map_rightUnitor equations to show that applying the functor to this counit and precomposing by its tensorator equals the transported counit precomposed by the inverse tensorator whiskered by F M.

The proved private helper monoidal_adjunct_isIso compares tensorRight D with the source internal-Hom functor and tensorRight (F D) with the target one using Adjunction.rightAdjointUniq. Apply the inverse target homEquiv to the proposed compatibility square; its left naturality, tensorator naturality, the rightAdjointUniq counit identities and monoidal_rigid_counit prove the square. Thus F(source identification) followed by the displayed mate equals inverse tensorator followed by target identification. These three maps are isomorphisms; IsIso.of_isIso_comp_left proves the displayed mate invertible. Apply this helper with the fixed canonicalTensorHomAdjunction on X and T and the pairing from step 1.

theorem perfect_internalHom_pullback_isIso
    [∀ Z : Scheme.{u},
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Z.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ (A : Type u) [Ring A], HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} A)]
    {T X : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ X)
    [∀ U : X.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (M K : schemeDerivedCategory X) (hM : Scheme.IsPerfect X M)
    (t : tensor (schemeDerivedCategory X) ⋙ derivedPullback g ≅
      (derivedPullback g).prod (derivedPullback g) ⋙ tensor (schemeDerivedCategory T))
    (ht : IsCanonicalPullbackTensorComparison g (fun E K => t.hom.app (E, K))) :
    IsIso
      ((canonicalTensorHomAdjunction T ((derivedPullback g).obj M)).homEquiv
        ((derivedPullback g).obj
          ((derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
            X.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj (op M, K))) ((derivedPullback g).obj K)
        (t.inv.app
            ((derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
              X.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj (op M, K), M) ≫
          (derivedPullback g).map ((canonicalTensorHomAdjunction X M).counit.app K)))
